newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: British-Tajik gold venture needs repairs.
newsitem.headline: British-Tajik gold venture needs repairs.

text.p: Darvaz, a British-Tajik gold venture, needs over $1 million of repairs to facilities damaged in an attack by armed Tajik rebels last year, an official said on Wednesday.
"Repair works have started already, and we hope the venture will resume its work in mid-March," Azim Dzhangiyev, deputy chairman of Tajikistan's State Committee on Precious Metals, told Reuters.
He said total damage to the venture, located in the south of the former Soviet republic, was estimated at $3 million and that repairs were being financed only by the Tajik side for now.
London-based Gold and Mineral Excavation Ltd has a 49 percent stake in the venture, while the remainder belongs to the Tajik government.
A unit of Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition damaged two concentrate plants, workers' houses and machinery during a raid in December 1996.
A Briton and a South African working for the venture were captured by the guerrillas and held for nearly three weeks before being released.
"Our British partner has assured us that it will continue cooperating with us despite this sad incident," Dzhangiyev said.
Since the set-up of the joint venture in November 1994, the British partner has invested about $3.5 million.

The venture had initially targeted production of two tonnes of gold a year, but independent analysts said that had not been achieved, with annual output at Darvaz "usually just a few hundred kilogrammes of gold".
